marks.gloss_en: if the rivals performed chalitza they are disqualified from the priesthood (the chalitza was needed)
Beit Shammai's reason: ״החוצה״ implies an inside (ervah) wife alongside the outside one, and the Torah says לא תהיה of the outside one -- the rival is released
kiddushin do not take hold in a yevama -- לא תהיה בה הויה לזר
once חוצה is written it is as if לחוץ were written, per R' Nechemya's rule on the locative he
any word needing a lamed prefix may take a he suffix instead (אלים-אלימה, מצרים-מצרימה)
Rav's rule (no kiddushin in a yevama) follows from לאיש זר, freeing חוצה
חוצה serves to include the betrothed woman (ארוסה) in the rule

Beit Shammai's reason is the principle that a prohibition does not take hold where another already exists: the sister-prohibition never lands, she is no ervah toward him, and her rival is an ordinary rival wife
challenge: where the surviving brother married first, the wife's-sister prohibition precedes the brother's-wife prohibition
answer: then the brother's-wife prohibition never lands, she carries no levirate bond, and the rival is a rival of an ervah where no mitzva applies -- permitted
